backlog: `Core\Str::replaceAll` copies its whole table into owned Rust `String`s on every call: 5 of the bench's 6 allocations per call come from a two-pair table. A borrowed table with one release at the end would remove them (priority 3; owner: `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/str.rs` module doc if taken up).

`Core\Str::replaceAll` checks every pair at every position, so its cost is text length × pair count × key length. Fine for small tables; the attack in `tests/hostile/core/Str/replaceAll/` sets the bound this goal measured.
